text:
maria (ml-eng): kicking off Ivy customer LoRA onboarding. attaching quick-eval results in thread. running sparse=0.7 LoRA + per-channel int3 quant. goal: preserve invoice amount formatting exactly.
aj (applied-ml): are we shadow-running on prod traffic or synthetic? :eyes:
maria (ml-eng): shadow on 5% prod + 1k-case Ivy-invoice quickpack. baseline run first.
shadowbot: shadow-roll started: policy=5% route=prod-eu model=redwood-4x-lora-sparse70-int3 run_id=sr-2026-03-22-001
sean (qa): paste the eval command you used so I can reproduce locally.
maria (ml-eng): local command:
```
python eval_pack.py --model redwood-4x-lora-sparse70-int3 --dataset ivy_invoice_quickpack.json --metrics amount_f1,format_accuracy,latency_p50
```
results snippet:
```
{"amount_f1":"0.942","format_accuracy":"0.88","latency_p50_ms":"82"}
```
nora (solutions): 0.88 format_accuracy is worrying 14 Ivy expects exact currency with two decimals. baseline redwood-4x was ~0.987, correct?
aj (applied-ml): baseline last week: amount_f1=0.971, format_accuracy=0.987, p50=94ms. sparse+int3 improved latency but regressed formatting.
maria (ml-eng): quick diff: model sometimes drops trailing zeros or changes separators when tokens cross LoRA-grafted attention patterns. examples in failing set show "$1,000.00" -> "$1,000" or "$1000.0".
sean (qa): attaching failing case ids: 17, 402, 889 (all trailing .00 or localized separators). will run extended locale tests.
shadowbot: traffic summary (first 10k reqs): 5xx=0, latency_tail down ~8%, format_mismatch_rate=0.12 vs baseline 0.01
nora (solutions): propose mitigations: 1) enable fallback for amount-sensitive routes, 2) re-run merge with lower sparsity (0.55) and limit graft to FF layers, 3) add token-preserve postprocess as interim. thoughts?
aj (applied-ml): agree. also test graft on FF-only vs FF+LN; LayerNorm grafting may be causing subtle token blending.
maria (ml-eng): plan: build sparse=0.55 FF-only LoRA, per-channel symmetric int3 quant, run quickpack and a 2% shadow run. deploy-bot schedule canary?
deploy-bot: canary scheduled env=dev->staging->prod-shadow percent=2 start=2026-03-22T15:42:00Z rollback_on=format_accuracy<0.95 or amount_f1<0.96
sean (qa): I'll add CI checks for exact formatted_amount match and regex for two-decimal currency. will block infra if any fail.
maria (ml-eng): uploaded artifact: s3://redwood-artifacts/ivy/redwood-4x-lora-sparse55-ff-only-int3.tar.gz sha256=3b7f1a...
aj (applied-ml): re-quantize note: use per-channel scales + symmetric zero-point; previous runs preserved formatting better.
maria (ml-eng): using that config now. commands: 
```
quantize --model orig.pt --out model-int3.pq --method per-channel --sym true
python eval_pack.py --model model-int3.pq --dataset ivy_invoice_quickpack.json
```
new results:
```
{"amount_f1":"0.964","format_accuracy":"0.956","latency_p50_ms":"78"}
```
nora (solutions): format_accuracy 0.956 meets our temporary gates (rollback threshold was 0.95) but still below baseline. with the postprocess guard we can proceed to shadow rollout and monitor closely.
sean (qa): I'll add locale packs (de, fr) and run KV-cache warmstart checks for long prompts (Ivy uses 4k). will surface any token offset regressions.
aj (applied-ml): please add a rollout note: "LoRA graft=FF-only sparsity=55% quant=per-channel int3 symmetric; fallback enabled for amount-sensitive endpoints."
maria (ml-eng): added to rollout doc + PR. final asks: assign 24h shadow monitoring (format_mismatch_rate, amount_f1, p99 latency). @nora?
nora (solutions): I'm on monitoring. will set alert: format_mismatch_rate > 0.03 -> pager.
maria (ml-eng): thanks. follow-ups I'll open separate threads: long-context KV-cache interaction, additional locale suites, and graft-layer ablation experiments. :white_check_mark:
